why: Puts the decode back outside a try, which is how the probe's handler shipped. decodeURIComponent throws URIError on malformed percent-encoding, and GET /% was measured killing the process with exit 1: nothing awaits an async request handler, so the rejection is unhandled rather than answered with a 500. The cost is not a security one -- it is a probe that answers a canvas census with a bare stack, at the moment someone is debugging a disposal leak. Exactly 1 of 9 fails, the malformed-encoding case; the traversal assertions are indifferent to this mutation, which is why they are separate entries.
